comparator.name: American Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026 intake takes 60 EC each year. Year two includes four rotating Special Topics courses. Year three includes a 30 EC minor or approved study abroad, a research seminar, a faculty-wide course and a thesis.
components: Americas I: The American Century and Beyond
Stories We Live By: Mediating Identities
The Americas III: From Exploration to Early Republic
Choose an eligible minor or apply for study abroad.
Choose one faculty-wide course. Published themes include humane AI, narrative, global change and cultural heritage.

core: United States and hemispheric history from early America to the contemporary period
American politics, democracy, institutions, political movements and global power
American literature, media, popular culture, rhetoric and cultural expression
Race, class, gender, religion, identity and inequality in American societies
Migration, transculturation and regional diversity across the United States, Canada and Latin America
Capitalism, consumer culture, trade, globalisation and technological change in the Americas
Interdisciplinary American-studies research, academic writing and independent inquiry
adjacent: American literature, media and cultural expression
American politics, identity and global affairs
Hemispheric migration, political economy and regional change
questions: How has American history shaped present identities, inequalities and social conflicts?
How do democratic institutions, political texts, movements and rhetoric shape American power?
How do literature, media and popular culture create and contest ideas of America?
How do migration, capitalism, globalisation and regional difference connect the Americas to the wider world?

candidates.label: U.S. Politics, Identity and Global Affairs
Hemispheric migration, political economy and regional change
candidates.assessment: UCR supports comparative empire, migration, identity, environmental justice and political economy through individual courses. The active curriculum does not sustain a dedicated Canada and Latin America sequence or a coherent additional hemispheric plan distinct from the selected directions.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match is complemented by two feasible generator-backed directions: American literature, media and cultural expression; and American politics, identity and global affairs. Each has a different organising logic, produces material curricular consequences and exceeds the pairwise 30-EC floor, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached. The separately assessed hemispheric migration and political-economy direction is not feasible as a 24-course Americas-focused programme because UCR lacks a sufficient regional sequence in Canada, Latin America and religion in the Americas; general global, economic and migration courses would not reproduce that target-specific direction.

alternatives.label: American History, Politics and Culture
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines American and modern history, political institutions and international relations with sociology, economics, literature, media, art, rhetoric and interdisciplinary research; the label therefore names its broad social, political and cultural composition.
alternatives.concept: Explore how U.S. history, democratic institutions and popular culture shape American society. Study gender and Indigenous histories, compare political systems, and investigate race and representation through media, literature and historical research.
progression: Historical, political, economic, rhetorical, literary, sociological and media foundations precede advanced work in Native American history, race and media, contemporary social theory, persuasion, documentary and historical research. Every formal prerequisite and planned-semester constraint is satisfied.

alternatives.label: American Media and Cultural Expression
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is organised around literary interpretation, American and global media, cultural history, visual art, race, rhetoric and creative production, so the label names the three dominant strands.
alternatives.concept: Explore how film, media, literature and art tell stories about American life. Begin with narrative and film analysis, study race and representation in American media, then use adaptation, documentary and creative work to examine how cultural meaning is made.
alternatives.distinctness: Seven courses in each direction differ from the broad plan. Film adaptation, literary theory, media history and art-historical methods shift the emphasis toward interpreting and making cultural works.
progression: Introductory literature, film and media, rhetoric, modern history, art history, sociology and research methods precede advanced literary theory, film adaptation, documentary, race and media, creative communication, persuasion and art-historical research. Every course is offered in its assigned term; no selected course has an unmet formal prerequisite.
traceOverrides: examines persuasion, framing, influence and communication ethics as cultural and media practices

alternatives.label: U.S. Politics, Identity and Global Affairs
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum concentrates political institutions and ideas, constitutional and international law, history, social movements, conflict, identity, race and the United States in global affairs.
alternatives.concept: Explore how U.S. power and identity develop through institutions, rights and social conflict. Study Indigenous histories, empire and social movements alongside comparative constitutional law and international relations.
alternatives.distinctness: Eight courses in each direction differ from the broad plan and fourteen from the media and culture plan. Constitutional and international law, rights, empire and social movements shift the emphasis toward political institutions and conflict.
progression: Modern history, comparative politics and Law, Society & Justice precede constitutional and international law; historical, political, sociological and research foundations precede advanced Native American history, race and media, social theory, conflict, social movements and historical research. Every formal prerequisite and planned-semester constraint is satisfied.

directly studies race, systemic racism, resistance and cultural power in American history and life
examines persuasion, framing, influence and communication ethics in political and public discourse

blocks: Groningen continues its dedicated Americas survey. UCR’s Modern History provides wider historical context.
Both examine modern U.S. history. Histories of Gender focuses on gender, slavery and lived experience.
Both examine Indigenous histories and colonization. Native American Histories follows these themes beyond the early republic.
Groningen requires a thesis. UCR’s historical research course culminates in a paper, and optional independent research is shown separately.
Both examine political institutions, parties and democratic participation. UCR compares political systems across countries.
Groningen studies political and media theory together. UCR studies contemporary social theory and media in separate courses.
Both guide students through a sustained research project. The UCR course focuses on historical inquiry and source criticism.
Groningen examines how stories shape identities. UCR offers related literary and media analysis.
Groningen compares societies and cultures across the Americas. UCR offers related work in history, politics and literary interpretation.
Choose a faculty-wide course in one of the published themes.
Both develop written and spoken argument. UCR emphasizes rhetoric and audience.
This course continues Groningen’s introduction to cultural theory.
Groningen introduces cultural analysis of race, class and gender. UCR explores these themes through sociology and history.
Both develop independent research through question design and analysis. UCR focuses on qualitative social research.
Choose an eligible minor or apply to spend a semester abroad.

notes.text: Groningen offers a continuous American Studies sequence across U.S. and hemispheric history, politics, literature and cultural theory. The UCR plans combine selected U.S. case studies with broader courses. The depth of coverage of Canada and Latin America differs.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

audience.programmeDescription: This English-taught bachelor studies U.S. history, politics and culture in the context of the Americas and the wider world.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR plans explore related questions through history, politics, media and culture, with different emphases in each plan.
